info.bio: Formado a principios de los 90's por Lisa marr (Voz, bajo) Robynn Iwata (Guitarra) y Valeria Fellini (Bateria) en Vancouver, Canada.  Luego de una serie de EP´s y split singles (Pep, Hot dog day, Volcano, etc.) sacaron su primera produccion en C.D. "Betty-Cola" que comprende todas las canciones de sus EP's anteriores más algunas nuevas canciones. Despues de varios discos y varios cambio de bateristas se disolvieron  a finales de los 90's.  Lisa Marr actualmente se presenta como LMX (lisa Marr Experiment)  y vive en Los Angeles, CA.

scenes.name: Hardcore en la era del punk-pop: emocore, ska-core y post-hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Mientras las revistas anuncian la «muerte del punk», el hardcore se convierte en un movimiento que no deja pueblo sin tocar y genera subgéneros. El «emocore» (Jawbreaker, Weezer, Sunny Day Real Estate, Promise Ring, At The Drive-In, Jimmy Eat World, Seaweed); el hardcore progresivo de Washington (Nation Of Ulysses, Make-Up, Shudder To Think, Jawbox, Edsel, Lungfish, Circus Lupus, Dismemberment Plan); el «ska-core» (Operation Ivy, Rancid, Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Sublime, No Doubt); el punk-pop que llega a las listas (Green Day, Offspring, Flop, Pennywise, Pegboy, Superchunk, Queers); el garage-punk californiano (Drive Like Jehu, Rocket From The Crypt, Blink 182, Zen Guerrilla); el jazzcore (Bazooka, Iceburn); la vieja escuela (D Generation, Supersuckers, Zeke, Dropkick Murphys, Silverfish, Turbonegro) y el post-hardcore de Unwound.

podcast.title: Childlike Stage Persona and Fan Interaction
podcast.body: CUB was renowned for their exceptionally sweet and childlike persona, which they consistently embraced. They frequently performed live shows in their pajamas and were known to bring gifts for their fans, meticulously working to present as childlike an image as possible in their music and stage presence. "They sometimes played shows in their pajamas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Cuddlecore Genre Creation
podcast.body: CUB, a band from Vancouver signed to Mint Records, developed and named their own genre, "cuddlecore," to describe their music. This genre encapsulated their melodic sound, jangly guitars, and a distinct childlike quality that they intentionally cultivated through their music and performances, often playing shows in pajamas and bringing gifts for fans. "Their music was melodic, it had the jangly guitars, and it had such a childlike quality to it that the band created a new genre for themselves."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
